title: Architecture standards: consolidated guidelines and ADRs
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and standards across API, coding, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It provides prescriptive guidelines, required templates, SLO thresholds, and the ADR (Architecture Decision Record) process for decisions that materially affect the platform. The goal is to create a single reference for engineers and cross-functional partners to ensure consistent, safe, and scalable design choices.

Scope

- Applies to all services and repositories owned by core product and platform engineering teams.
- Includes hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment controls where architecture differs.
- Does not replace team-level design docs; teams must cite and conform to these standards or document exceptions via ADRs.

Principles

1) Predictability: designs should yield predictable latency/cost behaviors.
2) Observability-first: all services must expose traces, metrics, and logs at defined granularity.
3) Incremental and reversible: favor rollouts that can be rolled back without data loss.
4) Cost-awareness: design choices must include unit-cost estimates for token and inference throughput.
5) Security by default: minimal privileges, encryption in transit and at rest where applicable.

Owners and governance

- Standards owner: Architecture and Standards team (eng-platform).
- Review cadence: Quarterly review or earlier if a critical outage or strategic shift occurs.
- ADR authoring: anyone may propose an ADR; authors must identify reviewers and an owner for implementation.

API Standards

Purpose: ensure a consistent, stable, and easy-to-use interface for internal and external consumers.

Required conventions:
- API surface design must follow RESTful resources + idempotent verbs for write operations. Where long-running or streaming operations are required, use gRPC or HTTP/2 streaming endpoints with clear reconnect semantics.
- All endpoints must include structured error codes (string code, message, http_status). Example: {"code":"quota_exceeded", "message":"token quota exceeded", "http_status":429}.
- Versioning: use major version in URL (/v1/...). Non-breaking changes may be added behind feature flags; breaking changes require a new major version and migration guide.
- Rate limiting and quotas: every API must expose per-customer rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset).
- Authentication: bearer tokens using our central auth service; token scope must be validated. Private deployments may support mutual TLS — document in deployment guide.

API Design Checklist (to include in PR):
1. Schema documented in OpenAPI (YAML).
2. Example request/response and error payloads.
3. Backwards compatibility analysis.
4. Latency expectations (p50/p95/p99).
5. Cost model estimate (tokens/compute per request).

Coding Standards

Purpose: maintain readability, security, and low operational burden.

Requirements:
- Primary languages: Go for core runtime/control plane, Python for tooling and evals, TypeScript for front-end/console.
- Linting: enforce golangci-lint, ruff/black/isort for Python, eslint+prettier for TypeScript.
- Testing: unit tests >= 80% coverage for critical components; integration tests required for API surface changes.
- Typing: use static typing (Go types, Python type hints with mypy, TypeScript strict mode).
- Error handling: return structured errors; avoid panics in long-running services.
- Secrets: never commit secrets; use vault and CI secret scanning.

Code Review Requirements:
- At least one reviewer from the owning service team and one reviewer from platform/security for changes affecting infra or security posture.
- PRs must include a brief performance impact assessment for any runtime-change.

Infrastructure Standards

Goals: predictable capacity, consistent networking, and secure multi-tenant isolation.

Network and Accounts:
- All cloud accounts and VPCs must follow the standard naming conventions and tags (team, env, owner, cost_center).
- Egress filtering by environment: prod must restrict egress by approved lists; non-prod should use broader but logged rules.

Provisioning and IaC:
- Terraform is the source of truth for infra. Repos must include a README with apply/plan pipeline steps.
- State: remote state in backend with encryption and state locking.
- Module policy: shared modules live in eng-infra/modules and are versioned semantically.

Capacity and Autoscaling:
- Capacity planning must include steady-state and peak estimates, with 99th-percentile queueing latency targets.
- Autoscaling policies must specify min/max nodes, target CPU/GPU utilization, and cooldown windows.

Model-serving Standards

Purpose: ensure safe, performant, and observable model inference across deployment modes.

Serving runtime requirements:
- Serve models using the platform runtime with support for continuous batching, KV cache management, and quantized kernels where applicable.
- Model artifacts must be packaged with a manifest (model_id, version, architecture, tokenizer, quantization_profile).

Model manifest (table):
| field | description | required | example |
|---|---|---:|---|
| model_id | canonical model name | yes | gpt-redwood-3b |
| version | semantic version | yes | 1.2.0 |
| architecture | transformer family | yes | causal-lm |
| tokenizer | tokenizer name | yes | sentencepiece |
| quantization_profile | profile name or none | no | q4_0 |

Rollout and compatibility:
1. Canary deployment to 1-5% of traffic for new model versions.
2. Monitor latency, error rate, and quality metrics (evaluation prompt set) for 24-72 hours.
3. Automated rollback triggers: +30% latency p95, +3% error rate, or regression in composite quality score > 2 points.

Quantization and kernel choices:
- Teams must benchmark a quantized variant and include a performance/cost/quality matrix in the model onboarding doc.
- Kernel selection recommendations should be recorded in profiling results; the runtime may override for stability.

Observability Standards

Goal: make failures and regressions easy to detect and diagnose.

Metrics:
- All services expose Prometheus metrics with standard labels: service, instance_id, env, model_id (where applicable), route.
- Standard metric names: request_duration_seconds (histogram), request_errors_total (counter), tokens_processed_total (counter), kv_cache_hit_ratio (gauge).
- SLI/SLO mapping must exist per service. Example SLOs:
  - API generation endpoints: availability 99.95% monthly; latency p95 < 450ms for baseline models.
  - Embeddings endpoints: availability 99.9%; latency p95 < 200ms.

Tracing and logging:
- Distributed tracing: use OpenTelemetry with 200ms sampling for baseline traffic and 100% sampling for error traces.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with a fixed schema: timestamp, level, service, component, trace_id, span_id, message, meta.
- Correlation: trace_id must propagate across async/work-queue boundaries.

Alerting and dashboards:
- Alerts must be actionable with runbook links. Avoid paging on transient or noisy metrics. Use multi-threshold alerts (warning/critical).
- Dashboards per service: Overview (latency/throughput/error), Model performance (quality, drift), Cost (tokens, GPU-hours).

Performance Standards

Targets and measurements:
- Define p50/p95/p99 latency goals per route and model class. Examples:
  - Small models (<=7B): p95 < 200ms; p99 < 500ms for generation with short contexts.
  - Medium models (7B-70B): p95 < 450ms; p99 < 1.2s.
- Throughput SLOs: tokens/sec per GPU and per model class must be established in benchmarking docs.

Benchmarks and perf-suite:
- Benchmarking must be reproducible: include commit hash, model artifact id, hardware profile, sequence length distribution, and batching policy.
- Use the central benchmarking harness (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) to record results.

Decision Records (ADRs)

Process:
1. Propose: create an ADR file in the architecture repo with title, context, decision, consequences, and links to tests/benchmarks.
2. Review: include at least two reviewers (one infra/platform, one product/owner).
3. Record: add ADR number and link to the consolidated ADR index page.
4. Implement: the owning team must track implementation tasks and schedule post-implementation review after 30 days.

ADR template (include as example in repo):
- ADR ID: e.g., ADR-2026-001
- Title: Short descriptive title
- Status: proposed | accepted | deprecated
- Context: problem statement and constraints
- Decision: chosen approach and why
- Alternatives considered: short pros/cons
- Consequences: migration, rollback, cost, security, observability implications
- Owner: team and contact
- Related pages/PRs: links

ADRs of record (examples):
- ADR-2025-010: Standardize on OpenTelemetry for tracing across environments.
- ADR-2025-021: Adopt continuous batching and KV caching in serving runtime.

Exception and change management

- Exceptions: must be documented via an ADR marked as "exception" and require approval from the Architecture and Standards owner and one engineering director. Exceptions auto-expire in 12 months unless renewed.
- Breaking changes: require a migration guide, deprecation timeline (>=90 days), and a rollback strategy.

Operational runbook pointers

- Incident playbooks must include: detection (metric thresholds), mitigation steps, rollback plan, and postmortem owner. See: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process.
- Capacity runbooks: scaling thresholds and contact list for manual capacity bumps.

Appendix: Templates and Examples

- Model manifest example:
{
  "model_id": "gpt-redwood-3b",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "architecture": "causal-lm",
  "tokenizer": "sentencepiece",
  "quantization_profile": "q4_0"
}

- ADR example header:
---
ADR-ID: ADR-2026-001
Title: Use semantic versioning for model artifacts
Status: accepted
---

Contact and feedback

For questions or to propose a change, open a PR against this document in the architecture repo and ping the Architecture and Standards owner (eng-platform). Regular office hours are held weekly — see the team calendar for details.

Change log
